title: Monster Academy

subtitle.text: It was Ben's first day of school at Monster Academy.
He floated into the auditorium for the first-day assembly.
Inside, he saw some other ghosts, along with a crowd of goblins, zombies, and other monsters.
Everyone was talking loudly.
"Ben, over here!"
Ben easily spotted the giant who was waving to him. Ben shot over to her.
"I'm glad you're here, Gaby," said Ben as he sat down next to her.
"You're the only one I know in—"
Crash!
Ben stopped talking. So did all the other monsters around him.
A two-headed monster looked up at the ceiling.
"What made that sound?" asked one of her heads.
"I don't know," answered her other head.
"It sounded like a giant landed on the roof of the school," said a goblin.
"Maybe it's my mom," Gaby whispered to Ben with a giggle.
Ben grinned. Gaby's mom was a giant, just like Gaby.
But Ben was pretty sure she wasn't on the roof of the school.
Mr. Freaky, the school principal, rushed onto the stage.
He was tall and thin, and he had three noses.
"Monsters, please be seated! Everything is totally under control!"
"Mr. Freaky loves to say that everything is under control," Gaby whispered.
"But what he really means is that everything is totally out of control!"
Ben laughed. It was lucky that his family had moved next door to Gaby over the summer.
Gaby had told Ben nearly everything he needed to know about Monster Academy.
"All the students and teachers are monsters, just like us," she had explained.
"The principal is pretty nice—as long as you don't get in trouble.
The office ogre is friendly too, unless she gets really busy.
After all, she only has four arms!"
Ben looked around the crowded auditorium again.
Most of the students were still talking.
A few ghosts in the last row were batting around a ball of paper.
Mr. Freaky clapped his hands for silence.
"Please don't worry about the loud crash. I'm sure it was just another broom."
A murmur went through the crowd.
"What is Mr. Freaky talking about?" asked a troll.
"We've had a few . . . incidents involving flying brooms this morning," Mr. Freaky went on.
"But let's forget about that for now.
Your eighth-grade class president, Waldo Wizz, would like to say a few words."
Monsters whistled and shouted as a young wizard approached the
microphone. Gaby's eyes lit up. "Waldo's amazing," she
gushed. "He's so cute. Plus, he's super smart, and he can do all kinds of
magic." Waldo waved to the
crowd. "This is going to be a fabulous school year," he
began. "We have two new after-school clubs—marching band and spell casting—and the first dance is coming up soon.
The Monster Mash dance will be held in a few weeks. So don't forget to show your best school spirit and participate in all our great activities!"
The crowd cheered again.
Waldo handed the microphone to Mr. Freaky.
"Settle down, students," said Mr. Freaky.
"Before you go to class, I have some news about People Place.
There's a new mayor."
"People Place is creepy," murmured a skeleton.
In the next row, a four-eyed monster leaned toward a three-eyed monster.
"I heard the new mayor is really scary looking. He only has two eyes!"
"Eww, gross!" replied the three-eyed monster.
Ben knew that Monsterville was next to a town inhabited by people.
A huge wooden fence separated the two towns.
His parents had warned him and his brother, Sid, to stay away from that fence.
But he didn't know anything about the mayor.
Mr. Freaky was still talking.
"I've been told that Mayor Hubbletree doesn't like monsters. So we must be extra careful not to upset him.
Remember—Monster Academy was built on land owned by People Place.
If we scare the people, they could force us to leave our school."
The two-headed monster raised her hand.
"I was near People Place last week," said one head.
"A human kid saw me and screamed!"
"I wasn't even doing anything!" said the other head.
Mr. Freaky nodded. "Unfortunately, some people get scared just looking at monsters.
Now, please exit quietly, monsters, and enjoy your first day of school.
It's going to be a wonderful school year!"
Ben and Gaby exchanged looks.
"And everything is totally under total control!" they said at the same time, laughing.
They headed out of the auditorium.
Ben thought it was fun to kid around with Gaby, and so far Monster Academy seemed really cool.
But he had to admit that a few things were worrying him.
The principal seemed nervous, and empty brooms were crashing around the school.
Plus, People Place had a new mayor—one who didn't like monsters!
Ben paused in the hallway to check his class schedule.
His first class was Cooking in room 103.
"Cooking class?" thought Ben. "I don't want to learn to cook!"
Around him lockers slammed and feet thudded as other monsters hurried to their classes.
"How does my eye makeup look?" Ben heard a purple monster ask a goblin.
"My mom says I put way too much on."
"It looks great," answered the goblin.
"But you missed your fourth eye completely."
Ben sighed and floated down the hall and into room 103.
He saw a zombie sitting alone at a table.
"Hi," said Ben. "Can I sit here?"
The zombie stared silently at Ben.
Ben felt uncomfortable. "Maybe he doesn't like me," he thought.
There hadn't been any zombies at his old school—mostly just other ghosts.
A witch sat down at the table. Ben recognized her from his homeroom.
She had flowing black hair and was dressed all in black.
Even her fingernails were painted black.
The witch smiled at Ben.
"Zombies just like to stare. It doesn't mean he doesn't like you."
"What?" Ben thought, startled. "How did she know what I was thinking?"
The witch laughed.
"I can't always tell what others are thinking, but sometimes I can. Have a seat."
"Uh-oh," Ben thought, sitting down.
He was going to have to watch his thoughts when this witch was around.
Ben sneaked another look at the witch.
Her eyes were green and flecked with gold.
She was the most beautiful witch he'd ever seen.
Just then a huge monster with two sharp horns stalked over to the table.
"Move over!" he growled at Ben. " I sit next to
Winnie!" "Chill out, Mog," said the witch, spreading her fingers to admire her nail
polish. Mog ignored her. He moved his face so close to Ben's that their noses nearly
touched. "Did you hear me?" said Mog. "I said, move
over!" The room was suddenly quiet. All the other monsters were looking at
Ben. Ben puffed out his chest, trying not to look
scared. "I heard you," he said. "But I'm not
moving." He glanced at Winnie, who was watching him with a surprised
look. Mog glared at Ben for a few
moments. Finally the big monster grunted and sat down on the other side of Winnie, at the end of the
table. To Ben's surprise, a ghoul sitting at the next table gave Ben the "claws-up" sign.
A moment later an old witch hobbled into the room.
She wore a crooked purple hat and orange sunglasses.
On her chin was a huge mole.
"She used to be the broom-flying teacher," Winnie whispered.
"My sister had her last year. She was terrible at flying brooms, though.
So now a new teacher, Miss Bungle, teaches it."
"Good morning, monsters," said the teacher.
"My name is Mrs. Hag, and I will be your cooking teacher."
Mog groaned.
"Excuse me!" said Mrs. Hag, fixing her eyes on Mog.
"Did you have something to say?"
"Yeah," said Mog. "I hate cooking."
"We actually have something in common," thought Ben.
Mrs. Hag grinned, revealing a row of brown, rotted teeth.
"Well then, Mog, perhaps you'll prefer cleaning.
That will be your job at the end of class."
Mog scowled, and Ben tried not to laugh.
After Mrs. Hag took attendance, she opened an enormous cookbook.
"For our first cooking lesson, we will make Slimy Toad Stew."
"Yum!" said the ghoul, smacking his lips.
"First we need to gather the ingredients." Mrs. Hag read from the cookbook.
"Let's see . . . Six rotten eggs, four dried worms, one ounce of bat claws.
Oh, I just bought some bat claws yesterday."
She felt in her pocket. "I thought I had them with me."
Mrs. Hag searched her other pockets, but she couldn't find the bat claws anywhere.
"Oh, well. I must have dropped them somewhere," she muttered to herself.
Mrs. Hag opened a cabinet and peeked inside. "What else can we use?
Aha! These thorns will probably work just as well as bat claws."
The teacher pulled a small bag from the cabinet.
"It says here that these are very special thorns," said Mrs. Hag as she examined the bag.
"They're from a bush that was grown by the light of the full moon."
"I'm not sure she knows what she's doing," Winnie murmured.
By now some of the monsters in class were starting to doze off.
Ben thought he heard the zombie snoring, but the zombie's eyes were still open. Ben looked at Winnie.
Winnie shrugged. "I don't know either.
He might be sleeping, or he might be awake. It's hard to tell with zombies."
Ben was about to respond when suddenly his stool flew out from under him and across the room!
Ben looked at his stool in surprise. It was halfway across the room.
Ben, however, was floating exactly where he'd been.
Mog lay sprawled on the floor. "He tried to knock me over!" Ben realized.
"Mog!" cried Mrs. Hag. "What are you doing?"
The monster got up off the floor. "I was, um, trying to get my stool back." He
pointed to the stool he had knocked across the room. "That's
not your stool," said Mrs. Hag. "That's
Ben's stool. Now sit down and behave yourself!" Mog
sat down as Ben got the stool. When
Ben came back, Mog leaned over the table, scowling at him. "Listen,
you pathetic excuse for a monster," Mog whispered. "Stay
away from Winnie, or you'll end up all alone, haunting a ghost town!" "Oh,
Mog," said Winnie. "He wouldn't be alone in a ghost town. Those
places are filled with ghosts." She flashed a smile at Ben. "Grr,"
snarled Mog, still glaring at Ben. "He's
a really nice guy," Winnie whispered to Ben. "He's just
not showing it today." Mrs. Hag
clapped her hands. "Let's start cooking! Mog, get
out the soap and scrub brush so you're ready to clean up when we're done." Ben watched
Mog get up. Ben had stood up to Mog earlier. But he
was new at school, and he couldn't afford to make enemies. He'd better
stay out of Mog's way for now. Then he
stole another quick look at Winnie, hoping she hadn't read his thoughts again. Maybe he'd
better stay out of her way too. * *
* At lunch Gaby told Ben more about the dance that Waldo had
mentioned. And over the next few days, that's all anyone was talking about at Monster Academy.
Who was going with whom to the Monster Mash dance?
Which girl monsters had asked boy monsters?
Why did the girl mummies always spend the evening giggling and running to the restroom to rewrap their bandages?
Ben wanted to go to the dance.
He had already met a bunch of girl monsters at Monster Academy.
But there was only one he really liked—and she was taken.
* * * A few days later during homeroom, Mr. Freaky
made an announcement. "Attention, monsters!" His voice crackled
over the loudspeaker. "As you know, we've been having some strange problems with our brooms
since school started. We've found brooms everywhere—the restrooms, the gym, the
soccer field. Just yesterday one crashed through my
office window!" "We're not sure who's causing the empty brooms to fly around, but we will find the
monster responsible. In the meantime, because of the danger, we're canceling all
extracurricular activities. That includes the Monster
Mash
dance." "What?" "That's
not fair!" Everyone in Ben's homeroom
started complaining. "Furthermore," continued Mr. Freaky, "all broom-flying classes will be suspended until the broom
incidents stop." "No broom-flying class?" shrieked a witch sitting next to Winnie.
"That stinks!" "You're not kidding." Winnie looked like she
might cry. "My parents promised to get me my own broom as soon as I got my broom-flying license." She
sighed. "I'll be an ugly old witch before I can fly a broom by myself."
"You could never be an ugly old witch," thought Ben as he gazed over at Winnie.
Winnie suddenly looked up, and her green eyes stared right into his.
Ben looked away quickly.
The bell rang, and all the students headed off to class.
As Ben drifted down the hallway, he thought about the sad look on Winnie's face again.
Poor Winnie. She'd looked so disappointed.
Suddenly Ben got a brilliant idea.
"I'll figure out who's crashing the brooms!" he thought.
"Then Winnie can go back to broom-flying class and get her own broom."
He was new at Monster Academy, but he could find the mysterious broom-flyer and help Winnie. He knew
he could. * *
* Later Ben heard a voice behind him in the
cafeteria. It was Gaby. He turned to look up at
her. "Guess what?" she cried, jumping up and down. The entire cafeteria
shook. "Hey, quit jumping!" complained a goblin at the next
table. "You spilled my toad
juice!" "What is it? Tell me!" said
Ben. Gaby stopped jumping. "Waldo Wizz asked me to go see a movie on Friday night!" she
said. "That's fantastic!" said
Ben. "Waldo is so nice," Gaby
gushed. "He's cute too. Have I told you about how great he is at
magic?" "Yes." Ben rolled his eyes.
Gaby had told him about Waldo Wizz's magic skills—along with his bright blue eyes—many, many times.
Ben was about to remind Gaby of this when another idea came to him.
Waldo was supposed to be some kind of genius at magic.
Maybe he could help find the monster who was crashing all the brooms.
Ben finally spotted Waldo in the hallway after English.
"Waldo!" called Ben, hurrying up to him.
Waldo spun around, sending his glasses flying off his nose.
He picked them up and peered at Ben.
"Hey, you're the new ghost . . . Ben, right?
How do you like Monster Academy so far?"
"It's great," said Ben. "Except for the crazy brooms crashing everywhere.
I was looking forward to the Monster Mash dance.
I hear it's always really fun."
"It is," Waldo agreed. "Too bad Mr. Freaky had to cancel it for now.
But don't worry," he went on. "I'm a pretty amazing wizard.
I can figure out who's flying the brooms in no time at all."
"Wow, that's great!" Ben said. "What are you going to do?"
"I'll formulate a truth potion," Waldo answered.
"I'll give it to every single student at Monster Academy and then question them, one by one."
"Oh . . . um . . ." Ben hesitated.
"There are hundreds of students at Monster Academy.
Won't it take a really long time to question everyone?"
"Hmm . . . I guess you're right . . . Hey!" Waldo suddenly had a big smile.
"You're a ghost! You could investigate without anyone seeing you!"
"I can move quietly," said Ben. "But I'm not invisible."
"Oh, right," said Waldo, rubbing his chin. "I know! I'll cast a sleep spell!"
"Okay," said Ben. This idea sounded a little better to him.
"When can we start?"
Waldo glanced around. "I can do the spell now if we hurry," he whispered. "Follow me!"
Ben followed Waldo into the empty library.
Waldo took an enormous book out of his backpack and flipped through the pages.
"Here it is," he said. "The sleep spell."
"Are you sure it will work?" asked Ben.
"I've never actually tried it," said Waldo.
"But don't worry—I'm very skilled at magic."
"That's what I've heard," Ben murmured.
Waldo quietly recited the spell.
When he was finished, he looked at Ben.
"The spell is done," said Waldo.
"Go look for clues. But be quick—the spell lasts for only one hour!"
Ben decided to search the broom-flying classroom first.
The room's closet was filled with witches' brooms.
Each one was marked "MA," for Monster Academy.
"I don't see any clues in here," he murmured.
"Just a bunch of—what's that?"
Ben reached down and picked up a small object.
"I wonder what this is," he thought, slipping it into his pocket. "It
looks a little like a tooth." Suddenly
a voice said, "What are you doing here?" Ben
spun around and saw Winnie. Her eyes were wide open. "Oh,"
said Ben. "I . . . uh . . ." Why
was Winnie awake ?
And what was she doing in the broom-flying classroom?
Winnie started talking really fast.
"I was in math class, but suddenly I just couldn't sit still.
No one could. I mean, who wants to do math when you feel like running or going flying or something? Right?
Even Mr. Slime didn't want to be there.
'Class dismissed!' he said, and then he ran out of the room so he could go jogging around the track."
Winnie ran over to the brooms. "Oh, how I wish I could fly them!"
"See you, Winnie," Ben called. She was acting really weird.
He had to find Waldo right away to see what was going on.
Earlier the halls had been empty.
Now teachers and students were rushing around.
In the middle of the chaos, Waldo made his way toward Ben.
"Something happened with the sleep spell!" whispered Waldo in a panic.
"Instead of putting everyone to sleep, it made them wide-awake!"
"You're not kidding!" said Ben. "What happened?"
Waldo looked sheepish. "I guess even a great wizard like me can make a mistake sometimes."
"I guess," Ben muttered.
Waldo held up his hands.
"Don't worry. I have another spell I can use. Follow me."
Ben followed Waldo to the library once again.
The wizard opened his big book of spells and recited some new words.
"This spell will make everyone forget everything that happens during the next hour," said Waldo.
"Even if other monsters see you snooping around, they won't remember."
"Awesome," said Ben. "Let's go search for clues!"
Ben and Waldo hurried back into the hallway.
Instantly all the monsters—students and teachers—fell silent.
They all stared at Waldo.
A purple monster ran up to Waldo.
"Oh, Waldo, what a wonderful wizard you are!"
A witch pushed the purple monster aside. "Waldo! You are so cute!"
"Will you marry me, Waldo?" shouted a mummy.
"Will you go to the Monster Mash with me?" cried a goblin.
"What is going on?" cried Ben.
"Why is everyone in love with you all of sudden?"
Waldo put his palm to his forehead.
"Ugh! I didn't cast a forgetting spell. I cast a love spell!"
To Ben's relief, Waldo's love spell didn't last long.
Soon everyone stopped fighting and arguing over Waldo.
"Students!" Mr. Freaky hurried down the hallway.
"Why are you all hanging around the hallway? Get to class!"
As the monsters started making their way back to their classrooms, Ben glanced at Waldo.
The wizard was scratching his head.
"I wonder why the love spell wore off so quickly. Maybe I did it wrong." "Who
cares why?" asked Ben. "Just be happy that it did. Otherwise,
you'd be married to everyone at Monster Academy by now!" "Let's
go back to the library," said Waldo. "I'm
sure I can come up with another spell." "Um
. . . No thanks." So far Waldo's magic wasn't much help. "Maybe
later," Ben added quickly. "Right now I'd better get to class." He
floated off, absentmindedly fingering the tiny toothlike thing in his pocket. "Now
what?" Ben thought. Maybe he needed to make a list of suspects. He
didn't really know many kids at Monster Academy, but already one of them was high on his list—Mog. Winnie
had said Mog was nice, but he seemed like a troublemaker to Ben. So
maybe Mog was the one causing all the trouble with the brooms. * *
* The next day at lunch, Mr. Freaky came into the cafeteria, looking even more nervous than
usual. His three noses were wiggling
wildly. "Everything is totally out of control!" he
cried. "Today two brooms are missing from the broom-flying
classroom. And we can't find them
anywhere!" Ben shot a look at Mog, who was sitting with
Winnie. But the monster wasn't looking his
way. The broom-flying teacher, Miss Bungle, was on lunch
duty. "Try not to get your noses in an uproar, Mr. Freaky," said Miss
Bungle. "You know what happens then—they all get stuffed
up." "How can I help it when someone keeps flying the brooms and crashing them all over school?" cried Mr.
Freaky. "It's a very dangerous situation!" He stopped to blow his noses.
"Until this problem is solved, I don't want to see anyone near the broom-flying classroom."
Ben glanced at Mog again.
Winnie was laughing at something the big monster was saying.
Suddenly Ben remembered that she'd come into the broom-flying classroom the day before. What was she—?
Abruptly, Winnie looked up and stared straight back at him.
Ben quickly looked down at his lunch tray.
He hoped she hadn't been reading his mind again.
Then she'd know all about his suspicions!
* * * That night Ben lay in bed, still thinking about Winnie and everything going on
at Monster Academy. The more he thought about the crashing brooms, the more suspicious he
was of Mog. "It can't be Winnie,"
he told himself. She was too nice. And besides, there was no reason for her to
cause trouble. But Mog, meanwhile, was
mean and— "Whoo!"
moaned Sid. "Sid!" Ben snapped. He looked over at his
younger brother. They had to keep the bedroom totally dark or Sid
got scared. Ben didn't mind
the dark. But tonight Sid was practicing his moaning, which made it hard for Ben
to think. "Whoo!" moaned Sid again. He was even louder
this time. "Sid, be quiet!" said Ben. "I'm trying
to concentrate." "Well, I'm trying to moan,"
said Sid. "I want to be really good at
it. Whoo!" Ben put his pillow over his head to muffle
the sound. Eventually, Sid stopped moaning and
fell asleep. Ben's parents had gone to bed too, so at last the house
was quiet. "Proof," thought Ben. "I need to find some
proof." Before long Ben had formed a
plan. He floated over to the window and quietly slid it
open. Careful not to wake Sid, he sailed out into the moonlit
night. Ben soared high above the streets of
Monsterville. Bats flew silently by, and the moon cast an eerie glow on the
rooftops. Ben looked nervously around. He hoped he didn't get
caught. Soon he was flying over Monster
Academy. The building was dark and empty. Ben knew he wouldn't be able to go
inside. He flew around the soccer field, looking for signs of the two missing magic
brooms. He checked the trash area and the bike rack, where Mog seemed to hang out a
lot. But there were no clues anywhere, as far as Ben could tell.
After that, Ben flew all around Monsterville, peering into alleyways, parks, and backyards as he looked for the missing brooms.
He saw a few brooms, but none of them was from Monster Academy.
He headed toward Mog's neighborhood, which was close to the fence that separated Monsterville from People Place.
Suddenly a loud, angry voice thundered below him.
"What do you think you're doing here?"
Ben recognized the voice right away.
It was Mog! There was a two-headed dog by his side.
"What are you doing here?" Mog demanded.
"I couldn't sleep," Ben said quickly. He landed in front of Mog.
"I was just flying around Monsterville."
"Just flying around?" Mog echoed.
He narrowed his eyes and moved closer to Ben. "Winnie loves to fly.
I bet you're looking for those two missing brooms to impress her!"
Ben was surprised that Mog had guessed the truth so quickly.
He backed away from the big monster.
"No, I'm just flying around," he repeated.
Suddenly Mog smiled. "I'm just kidding," he said.
"I'll tell you a secret, but you have to promise not to tell anyone, not one single monster!"
"Why is Mog being so friendly all of a sudden?" Ben thought.
He was suspicious, but aloud he said, "I won't tell."
"Come closer," said Mog. "I have to whisper so no one will hear."
"But there's no one here but us," said Ben.
"You never know," said Mog, glancing around.
"There could be spies on either side of the fence."
Ben hovered so he was at eye level with Mog.
"Closer!" hissed Mog.
Ben moved closer.
"I've been looking for the missing brooms too," Mog whispered.
"I think people are stealing them."
"What?" Ben felt his eyes widen. "Why do you think that?"
"I was sneaking around in People Place the other day," said Mog.
"I saw two brooms on the roof of a house.
I couldn't climb up to get them, but I could clearly see 'MA' on the handles."
Ben peered at Mog in the moonlight. Was he telling the truth?
"Why would people steal the brooms?" asked Ben.
"And how could they make them fly?"
"I don't know." Mog shrugged. "Maybe it's because the brooms are magic.
The people are probably jealous and want to learn how to fly them.
And that's why the brooms are crashing all over the place.
The people don't know what they're doing."
Ben still didn't trust Mog.
"If people did steal the brooms, why did they put them on a roof?
That doesn't make sense."
Mog shrugged again. "They probably just thought it was a good hiding spot.
After all, who would think to look up on a roof?"
"That makes sense," said Ben.
"So did you tell Mr. Freaky you saw the brooms?"
"No," said Mog. "I didn't want to get in trouble for sneaking around People Place."
He paused and seemed to think for a moment. "You're a ghost, though.
You could easily fly into People Place and get the brooms back."
Ben looked suspiciously at Mog. Could he really trust this monster?
"Listen," said Mog. "If we get those brooms back, we can put them in the broom closet.
Then, as long as they don't disappear again, Mr. Freaky will probably change his mind about the Monster Mash dance.
And you know Winnie will be happy."
Ben thought about this. Mog might be telling the truth.
Then again, Mog was probably lying. Maybe he wanted to get Ben in trouble.
Mog certainly wouldn't want Winnie to feel grateful to Ben.
Still, it couldn't hurt to fly over People Place just to see the brooms, could it?
Finally Ben nodded. "Okay, I'll do it. Where's the house?"
"Awesome," said Mog with a grin.
"It's a big house on Main Street. It's only a few blocks from the fence.
The house is yellow, and it has a tower. You can't miss it."
Ben took a deep breath. "I'll be back soon."
"I'll be waiting right here," whispered Mog as Ben flew off.
Ben couldn't believe he was actually flying over the fence and into People Place.
On the other side, he looked around.
Without any people, the town looked a lot like Monsterville, with schools and stores and parks.
Still, Ben knew he couldn't spend too much time looking around.
If he got caught, he'd be in serious trouble.
Ben flew a bit farther and found Main Street.
It was lined with houses, and cars were parked along the street.
He quickly spotted the yellow house with the tower.
He flew over it, but he didn't see any brooms on the roof.
"Mog definitely lied to me," thought Ben.
There were no brooms from Monster Academy here.
Ben was hovering outside a window when he noticed a young boy inside.
The boy was fast asleep in bed, hugging a giant stuffed teddy bear almost as big as Ben.
Suddenly there was a loud crashing sound from back by the fence.
A couple of lights in nearby houses blinked on.
The boy sat bolt upright in bed.
He stared directly at Ben and shrieked, "Mommy! Daddy! A ghost!"
A light in the yellow house blinked on, and Ben heard the sound of footsteps racing up the stairs.
A deep voice boomed, "What's wrong, son? Don't worry! Daddy's coming!"
Ben gulped. "I'm going to be in big trouble!"
Too scared to find out what would happen next, Ben shot back toward Monsterville as fast as he could.
Several garbage cans near the fence had been knocked over.
Ben flew over the fence and then stopped to catch his breath.
"That was scary," thought Ben. "That little kid was so scared of me!
I could have gotten in a lot of trouble!"
Looking around, he realized Mog was nowhere in sight.
"Mog!" called Ben. "Mog, where are you?"
There was no answer.
"Where did he go?" Ben murmured.
Then he remembered the loud crashing sound and the garbage cans that had been knocked over.
Could Mog have done that? Ben wondered about it as he flew home.
A short while later, Ben slipped back into his bedroom.
Sid was still snoring quietly in his bed.
Ben climbed into his own bed, his heart still racing as he thought about his adventure in People Place.
What if he'd been caught? He wasn't sure what would have happened.
Maybe the people would have captured him.
First thing in the morning, they probably would have marched him over to Monster Academy and into Mr. Freaky's office. Yikes!
Ben shuddered and tried to go to sleep, but it wasn't easy.
He tossed and turned all night.
He couldn't stop thinking about the little kid he'd scared.
And he couldn't stop thinking about Mog.
"I knew I never should have trusted him," thought Ben.
The next morning at school, Ben spotted Mog in the crowded hallway before homeroom.
He stormed toward him. "Where did you go last night?" he called.
To Ben's surprise, Mog shot a quick glance at Ben and then hurried off in the other direction.
Ben narrowed his eyes at the monster.
"Mog definitely knocked over those garbage cans.
I'm sure he was just trying to get me in trouble!
Well, he can't hide from me forever.
He'll have to talk to me in cooking class."
Ben went to homeroom and sat down, still fuming.
"Attention, all monsters!" Mr. Freaky's voice crackled over the loudspeaker.
"A very grave situation has come to my attention!"
"Uh-oh!" Ben bolted upright, worried.
But a ghost sitting next to Ben was laughing.
"A 'grave' situation? Ha-ha!
Maybe we're going to take a field trip to a graveyard!"
"Oh, I love graveyards!" said a skeleton girl dreamily.
Mr. Freaky was still talking. "First period is canceled this morning.
Instead I want all students to report to the auditorium."
Ben's thoughts were racing.
Did Mr. Freaky know about his adventure in People Place the night before?
Ben remembered that little kid and how scared he'd looked at the sight of a ghost.
Why in the world had Ben listened to Mog?
The bell rang just then, and monsters began to stream out of homerooms to make their way to the auditorium.
Ben followed them and slunk into a seat next to Gaby. "Hey," he murmured.
"I wonder what Mr. Freaky is going to talk about," said Gaby.
Ben was too worried to respond.
The principal walked up to the microphone, looking very serious.
"I received a phone call this morning," said Mr. Freaky.
"Apparently a ghost flew into People Place last night and scared a little child."
A shocked rumble went through the auditorium.
"A ghost?" said a fish monster.
"In People Place?" said an octopus monster.
"Scared a kid?" said a purple monster.
"That's terrible!" said Gaby.
Ben slid down in his chair, holding his breath.
"Quiet!" shouted Mr. Freaky.
Right away the entire auditorium fell silent.
"Unfortunately the child who saw the ghost isn't just any child," said Mr. Freaky.
"He's Mayor Hubbletree's son!"
Ben almost slid off his chair. The mayor's son?
Had Mog known that when he sent Ben to that house to look for the brooms?
Ben saw Mog sitting in the next row, but the monster was looking the other way.
"As many of you know," said Mr. Freaky, "Monster Academy was built on land owned by People Place."
The principal looked at the floor and took a deep breath.
"There's no easy way to say this, but . . .
Mayor Hubbletree has decided to evict us."
A huge gasp filled the auditorium.
"That means we must leave," said Mr. Freaky.
"Monster Academy is going to be destroyed!"
At first Ben had been afraid of getting in trouble for scaring the little boy.
Now something much worse was happening.
Mayor Hubbletree was planning to destroy Monster Academy.
And it was all Ben's fault!
"Maybe I should confess," thought Ben in a panic.
Maybe if he told Mr. Freaky the truth, the principal could find a way to get Mayor Hubbletree to change his mind about the school.
But Ben wasn't sure.
He was new at Monster Academy and still learning how things worked there.
Maybe he'd just better stay quiet for now.
At lunch that day, Ben wanted to be alone to think. He
found a table with two zombies and sat down. While
the zombies stared and drooled silently on their food, Ben thought about his situation. Nearby
he heard Winnie talking. "I
can't believe Mayor Hubbletree is going to destroy Monster Academy," she said. "What's
going to happen to us? Where will we go to school?" "Believe
it!" a mummy replied. "And
just wait until he finds the ghost who scared his son. That
ghost is going to be in big trouble!" Ben
looked over at Winnie. To his surprise, she smiled at him! Ordinarily
Ben would have been thrilled, but today he had too much on his mind. "I
have to find Mog," he thought. Once
he talked to Mog, Ben could make a plan, figure out what to do. * *
* But Ben didn't have a chance to talk with Mog until the next morning in cooking
class. Mrs. Hag assigned the two of them to make a rotten-egg omelet
together. "Mog!" Ben growled as soon as they were alone at their cooking
station. "You got me into
trouble!" "It wasn't my fault," said Mog. He cracked a rotten egg into a
bowl. "What do you mean, it wasn't your fault?" Ben glared at the big
monster. "I know you knocked over those garbage
cans. You made a big loud sound just to get me in
trouble. And you're probably the one who's flying the
brooms!" "Monsters, quiet!" snapped Mrs.
Hag. "You're supposed to be cooking, not
talking." Ben lowered his
voice. "You knew the big house with the tower was the mayor's mansion.
I'll bet you never saw any witches' brooms on the roof.
You just wanted to get me into trouble because Winnie is nice to me!"
Mog's shoulders slumped. "Okay," he said. "You're right.
I made the whole thing up to get you in trouble.
The brooms were never on the roof. I knocked over the garbage cans.
But I just wanted you to get in a little bit of trouble.
I didn't know the whole thing would turn into such a big deal."
Ben noticed Winnie glancing over at Mog as the monster spoke.
"Well, it is a big deal!" Ben whispered furiously.
"What's going to happen once they find out it was me who entered People Place?
That was your plan.
So you'd better help me find a way to fix the problem it caused!" Mog
nodded slowly. "You're right, Ben," he said. "I'm
really sorry. But I'm not the one who's taking the brooms, I swear." Ben
nodded. For the first time, Mog actually seemed sincere. He
was pretty sure Mog was telling the truth. "Meet
me outside after school, by the flagpole," Mog said. "We'll
come up with a plan together." *
* * After school Ben hurried outside. He was shocked by what
he saw. Several large construction vehicles sat in front of
the school. A big bulldozer rumbled loudly,
puffing smoke. In front of the vehicles stood a man dressed in a
dark suit. A few other people stood
behind him. "That must be Mayor Hubbletree,"
thought Ben. Mr. Freaky ran out of the school, waving his arms
frantically. "Mayor Hubbletree!" cried the principal. "What are you
doing?" "I told you yesterday, Freaky," said the
mayor. "I'm knocking this place to the
ground!" "I didn't know you meant so soon!" said Mr.
Freaky. "We need time to move our things
out!" "The ghost who scared my little boy should have thought of
that!" Mayor Hubbletree shot
back. "Mayor, please," said Mr.
Freaky. "Over two hundred monsters attend Monster
Academy. Where will they go to school? Can't you at least wait until next
week?" Mr. Freaky's lip began to
tremble. Ben thought the principal was about to
cry. The mayor sighed. "Oh, all
right. I'll give you one more day. But that's
all!" Ben found Mog and rushed over to him. "Did you hear that?" asked

Mog shook his head. "I can't think fast."
Ben was about to say something, but Mog put up a claw.
"I can think slowly though," he said. "And I have an idea."

Ben stared at Mog in disbelief. Mog wanted to sneak back into People Place?
"Let me finish," said Mog.
"I think we should sneak into People Place, go to Mayor Hubbletree's house, and apologize."
"What?" Ben's jaw dropped.
He had imagined telling Mr. Freaky what had happened.
But he'd never imagined speaking directly to the mayor! "It's
the right thing to do," Mog went on. "I'll
tell him the truth. And I'll explain that I tricked you." Just
then Winnie stepped out from the crowd, her eyes flashing with anger. "I

through!" said Winnie. "Even
if the school was still having the dance, I wouldn't go with you. Not

spun around and walked away. Mog
stared after her and sighed. "We'd
better do something fast," he murmured. *
* * That evening Ben and Mog met by the fence between Monsterville and People
Place. Mog couldn't fly, so Ben waited while he climbed the
fence. Halfway over, Mog let out a
yelp. "Uh-oh," said Mog. "I'm
stuck!" "How are you stuck?" said
Ben. "My pants are caught on a nail," said Mog. "Hold on a
second." The monster tried to lift himself to free his pants, but he
slipped.
Rip! Ben tried not to laugh as Mog hung from the nail by his ripped
pants. "Ugh!" cried Mog. "This
is—" Rip! Mog's pants ripped some more, and then he fell to the
ground.
"Ouch!" "Are you okay?" asked
Ben. Mog rubbed his head. "Yeah, I'm
okay." He stood up, and his pants fell down. "Aw, man! My pants are ruined!"
"Never mind that now," said Ben. "Let's just get this over with."
Ben and Mog hurried toward the mayor's house.
Mog had to hold up his pants as he ran.
The sun was setting, and the streetlights were beginning to flicker on.
Soon Ben and Mog were standing in front of the mayor's house.
"What do we do now?" asked Ben.
"We go up to the door and knock," said Mog.
Ben gulped. "You first," he said.
They went to the door, and Mog knocked with one hand.
The other hand was still holding up his pants.
Ben's heart beat faster as he heard heavy footsteps getting closer. The
door finally opened, and Mayor Hubbletree was standing there. "Monsters!"
cried the mayor. "What are you doing here?" "Hello,
s-sir," Ben stammered. "We, uh—" "Monsters?"
cried a little boy's voice. Ben
gulped as the mayor's son ran to the doorway. "Oh
no!" thought Ben. "He'll see us and get scared all over again!" It
was too late. The
boy stood in the doorway and stared, wide-eyed, at Mog and Ben. He
looked like he was going to scream. Mog
held up his hands and said, "Don't be scared!" Instantly
his pants fell down. "Ha-ha!"
The boy laughed hysterically. Mog's
face turned red as he quickly pulled his pants back up. "Sorry about
that, I—" "That's funny!"
said the boy. "Ha-ha!" Mayor Hubbletree
had been frowning. But as
he watched his son laugh, his frown faded. Soon he
was smiling. Then he was laughing. Ben looked
from the boy to the mayor to Mog. Despite being

laughed too. * *
* The next day at school, Ben heard lots of kids talking about him and
Mog. "I heard Mog and Ben went to Mayor Hubbletree's house last night," said a
ghoul. "Yeah," said a troll. "I heard Mog's pants fell
down." "It's a good thing they did," said a purple monster.
"The mayor's son thought it was funny.
The mayor isn't angry at monsters anymore."
A mummy nodded. "Yep. And now he's no longer planning on destroying Monster Academy."
Ben also overheard that Mayor Hubbletree wasn't just going to leave Monster Academy alone.
"I'd like to see monsters and people get along," the mayor had told Mr. Freaky.
"Maybe our students could take a field trip to Monster Academy."
"That would be wonderful," said Mr. Freaky.
"And I'm sure our monsters would love to see People Place."
Ben was floating along the school hallway as monsters gathered around to congratulate him.
"Way to go, Ben!" shouted a ghoul.
"Thanks," said Ben. "It was really Mog's—" Suddenly—
crash! A broomstick smashed through a wall!
Mr. Freaky rushed into the hallway.
He moaned when he saw the broomstick in the wall.
"Who is doing this? It has to stop!"
Ben cringed. He knew now it wasn't Mog stealing the brooms.
So there was only one other suspect—Winnie.
The next day in cooking class, Mrs. Hag was explaining the importance of using the best ingredients.
Ben tried to listen, but he was distracted by his worries about Winnie.
And his worries that Winnie would know what he was thinking.
"Everything should be moldy or rotten," Mrs. Hag told the students.
"Some cooks like to use fresh ear wax and pocket
lint."Ben didn't have any ear wax, so he reached into his pocket to see about
lint. He felt the tooth he'd found in the broom flying classroom and took it out of his
pocket. Mrs. Hag spotted it as she walked past Ben's
worktable. "Oh, you've got a bat
claw. I bought some the other day, but I can't find
them. I guess I lost them
somewhere." Ben was stunned. The object in his palm wasn't a tooth; it was a bat claw!
Had Mrs. Hag accidentally dropped one in the broom-flying classroom? Could she be . . . ?
Did that mean Winnie . . . ?
"Oh, wow," Ben murmured.
He had to tell Mr. Freaky! But Ben knew he needed proof before he accused a teacher of anything.He
glanced at Mog. Maybe Mog would help him. They
weren't exactly friends now, but they weren't enemies anymore either. At
the end of the day, Ben found Mog in the hallway. "Mog!
I need to talk to you." "Sure,"
said Mog. "What's up?" "I
think Mrs. Hag is the one flying the brooms," whispered Ben. "Really?"
said Mog. He looked shocked. Ben
filled him in. "It
makes sense," said Mog. "Winnie
told me Mrs. Hag was really upset when Mr. Freaky made her stop teaching broom flying. And
everyone says she's terrible at flying. That
could explain the crashing brooms." Ben
nodded. He was getting more and more excited about his theory. "Now
we just need to prove it." "Let's
look for clues in the broom-flying classroom," said Mog. The

retirement. It turned out that she'd been making trouble at school to get back at Mr.
Freaky. Ben didn't think anyone at Monster Academy was sorry to see Mrs. Hag
go. Mr. Freaky had already hired a new cooking teacher, and Miss Bungle was going to start teaching broom flying
again. Later Gaby rushed up to Ben in the

Winnie and Mog had broken up! Now he could ask Winnie to the dance!

"Maybe she won't say yes," he thought.

Outside, he could see Winnie soaring over the soccer field on one of the school brooms.
She was leaning over it with a happy look on her face, probably thrilled to be flying again.
"Here goes." Ben took a deep breath and then headed toward her.
Ben floated out to the soccer field where Winnie was flying her broom.
She looked so happy soaring over the field.
"I'm coming in for a landing!" he heard her say.
"Me too!" cried another witch, tilting her broom down toward the field.
Ben watched Winnie cruise to a soft landing.
Then he floated over to her, his heart beating fast.
He had come outside to ask her to the Monster Mash dance on Friday night.
"What if she says no?" Ben thought, suddenly panicked.
That would be terrible.
He'd feel so stupid, and then things would get awkward between them. Maybe he shouldn't—
Just then Winnie smiled at him. Her green eyes sparkled in the sunlight.
Ben smiled back nervously. Winnie could sometimes read people's thoughts.
Did she know what he was thinking now?
"Great flying, Winnie," said Ben quickly.
"Thanks," she answered. "I'm practicing for my broom-flying test.
If I pass, I'll finally have my broom-flying license.
Then maybe I can join the Witches' Formation team.
They get to fly over the school during important events."
"I'm sure you'll pass," said Ben.
He knew he had to ask her now, before he lost all his courage.
He took a deep breath—such a deep breath, he suddenly felt dizzy.
Winnie stared at him. "Ben, are you okay? You look pale, even for a ghost."
"I'm fine," Ben lied.
His heart pounded faster. "Winnie, will you . . . um . . . ?"
Smiling, Winnie tilted her head. "Will I . . . ?"
"Will you go to the Monster Mash with me?"
For a moment Winnie didn't say anything.
"Oh no!" Ben thought, panicking again. "I never should have—"
"I'd love to," she said.
"You would? I mean, wow! That's great!"
Suddenly Ben didn't know what to say. "Dancing is fun, right?"
"I love dancing," Winnie agreed.
"I love it almost as much as I love broom flying."
"Me too," said Ben. "I mean, not broom flying but just regular flying.
Not that there's anything wrong with broom flying. It's just that I'm a ghost and . . ."
"What a dumb thing to say," Ben thought as Winnie giggled.
He was babbling like an idiot.
"I'll pick you up at seven," Ben told her. "Okay?"

So I have to get to the gym early to help decorate.
Maybe we can just meet at the dance?"

"Okay," said Winnie, grinning at him.
Ben floated away as fast as he could. He could not believe his good luck.
Ever since he'd first seen Winnie, he'd thought she was the most beautiful witch in the world.
And now she was going to the dance with him!

"Good morning, students.
I wanted to let everyone know that Miss Bungle is out sick with the flu today.
So all of her broom-flying classes and activities are canceled until she returns. Thank you."

Their first Monster Mash dance together was going to be perfect.
That night the moon shone bright and full.
Ben headed over to Monster Academy early.
"What a fantastic night," he said to himself.
"There will be great music, great food, and a whole night with Winnie!"

"Wow!" he burst out.
Silky spider webs shimmered from the ceiling, and eerie lights cast spooky shadows around the room.

Ben stepped out into the hallway.
"Hey, Ben!" Waldo Wizz called. "You're here early."

I thought I'd come early to help her."

Near them a small appliance that looked like a pressure cooker beeped noisily.
Waldo rushed to the back of the lab.

Then he thought about Winnie in her beautiful new black dress.

He frowned at all the buckets lined up onstage.
"And I make sure our schools are in good shape.
As you can see, being mayor is the most important job of all."
"Thank you for coming, Mayor Hubbletree," Mr. Freaky said quickly.
"I'm sure you have an important meeting to get to now."
As the students applauded, the mayor spoke softly to Mr. Freaky.
But Ben could hear his voice come through the microphone.
"I'll talk to you later, Freaky," the mayor muttered.
"It looks like we have a crisis here."
"Crisis?" Ben thought.
Before he could say anything to Winnie, the final guest scurried onto the stage.
It was a dust collector carrying a broom.
Waldo started sneezing again as clouds of dust drifted from the stage.
The dust collector straightened his rags.
"My job is very exciting," he said in a flat tone.
"I collect dust. I begin sweeping at dawn and . . ."
"Time for a nap," Mog whispered, shutting his eyes.
"I'm not interested in dust collecting."
Finally the dust monster was finished, and Mr. Freaky returned to the microphone.
"I hope you enjoyed Career Day, students. We—"
Just then the auditorium door banged open, and a skeleton clattered into the room.
He had a long black beard and wore an eyepatch like a pirate.
His other eye burned like fire as he waved a gleaming sword and snarled.
"Give me all your gold!"
The pirate skeleton clattered onto the stage, knocking over two buckets as he swung his sword.
"Hand over all your loot, monsters!" the skeleton demanded.
"Agh!" Mr. Freaky screamed and darted behind a stage curtain.
Waldo was shaking.
"B-but all we have is our lunch money!" he said.
"Huh?" The noise suddenly woke Mog from his nap.
"What's going on? Are we being robbed?"
"Robbed? Ha!"
The bearded skeleton roared, waving his sword in Mog's direction.
"You're being pirated!
I'm Pirate Pedro, and I'm here to tell you all about my career—pirating!"
Mr. Freaky peeked out from behind the curtain.
"You mean you're part of Career Day?"
"Yes, and I'm the best part of Career Day," Pirate Pedro said.
"Because the best career in the world is being a pirate!"
"Whoa." Mog sat up in his seat with wide eyes. "Cool!"
"Being a pirate isn't for everyone," Pedro went on.
"You have to be strong.
You have to be bold.
Most of all, you have to be brave.
I'll never forget my first voyage as a captain of a pirate ship.
I sailed for the king.
He sent my crew and me to track down the most feared pirate on the sea.
He was called Awful Ollie the Orange."
"Ooh! Ooh!" Mog waved his hand in the air to ask Pedro a question.
"Was he called Ollie the Orange because his hair and beard were orange?"
"No. His hair and beard were yellow.
But he wore lit candles in them.
His whole face looked like it was on fire."
"Did you ever track down Ollie?" Ben asked.
"Oh yes," Pedro said.
"We found Ollie and battled him and his men for a day and a night.
Cannonballs flew from our pirate ships.
But finally my crew managed to board Ollie's ship and capture him and his crew.
We threw Ollie to the sharks, and then my merry band and I claimed his treasure."
"Yay!" Monsters cheered. "Treasure!"
"But the king betrayed us," Pedro went on with a scowl.
"He stole our treasure for himself."
"That stinks," Mog said.
Water suddenly gushed from the ceiling, and Pedro ducked out of the way.
Mr. Bog ran up to the stage with more buckets.
"This is ridiculous," Ben whispered to Winnie.
"They'd better fix the leaks soon."
"I heard Mr. Freaky talking to the office ogre before the assembly.
Mr. Freaky said there's a budget crisis.
So there's not enough money to fix the roof."
Winnie looked worried.
"Ben, what if Monster Academy has to shut down?"
"That won't happen," Ben said.
"I'm not so sure," Winnie said.
"Things sound bad. I'm really worried about it."
Meanwhile, Pedro was still telling his adventure story.
"Eventually my band and I managed to steal the king's ship and sail away.
We sang merry songs as we plundered the seven seas.
And whenever we found the king's ships, we sent them to Davy Jones' locker!"
"I got stuffed into my locker once," a blob said.
"It was very uncomfortable."
Waldo laughed.
"Davy Jones' locker isn't really a locker.
It's just an expression that means the bottom of the sea."
"I've been to the bottom of the sea!" a fish monster cried.
"It's awesome!"
"On the sea we battled zombie whales and killer crabs," Pedro went on.
"Then Awful Ollie the Orange came back as a ghost.
We had to fight him again and again.
When it was all over, we sang songs of our victories."
"Finally . . ." Mog looked dreamy.
"I've found the perfect career—pirating!"
Everyone had lots of questions.
"Pedro, are you still a pirate?" Cleo asked.
Pedro shook his head.
"No, I'm retired now.
I spent almost a hundred years in jail.
By the time I got out, everything had changed in Monsterville."
He sighed.
"Pirating has changed a lot too.
It's not what it used to be."
Mog waved his hand again.
"You must have gotten super rich from all that treasure."
Pedro grinned, flashing a shiny gold tooth.
"I had huge piles of gold," he boasted.
"I had pearls the size of your head!"
"Wow!" The students were impressed.
"What happened to all your treasure?" Gaby asked.
Pedro frowned.
"The police confiscated most of it when they locked me up.
But they didn't get all of it.
I managed to hide my most valuable treasure."
"That's good," Mog said.
"Where did you hide it?"
Pedro hesitated.
Then he looked sad as he shrugged.
"I can’t remember!"
All the monsters in the auditorium gasped.
"What? Seriously?" Ben said. "You lost your treasure?"
"Did you bury it somewhere?" Mog asked.
"Of course I buried it!" Pedro said.
"I'm a pirate. That's what we do—we bury treasure."
"Did someone find it and dig it up?" Cleo asked.
Pedro scratched his head.
"I don't think so. I mean, a lot of people knew about our treasure.
A local artist even painted a picture of the burial.
But I have no idea what happened to the treasure chest.
As I said earlier, I was in jail for a long time.
By the time I got out, Monsterville had completely changed.
There were new streets and buildings.
I had no idea where I'd buried my loot.
And neither did anybody from my pirate band."
Mog looked confused. "Don't pirates usually make treasure maps?" he asked.
"Why didn't you do that?"
"I did make a map," Pedro replied. "But—"
"Ah-choo!" Waldo sneezed loudly, spewing large green bugs into the air.
Winnie swatted a few bugs away from her hair.
"Do you still have the map, Pedro?" she asked.
"I think somebody stole it!" another monster blurted out.
"I don't have the map anymore." Pedro shook his head sadly.
"I buried my treasure that day and then I went back to sea.
But our crew soon got into a big battle with another ship.
Our pirate ship caught fire and . . ." Pedro gulped.
"The treasure map burned. I tried to save it, but . . ."
Tears streamed down his face. "It was no use."
"Have you tried looking for the treasure in Monsterville?" Mog asked.
Pedro nodded. Mr. Freaky handed him a handkerchief, and the pirate wiped away his tears.
"Yes. When I got out of jail, I searched for the treasure for several years.
But it was hopeless." He shook his head.
"It was the best loot my merry band and I ever got.
And all I have now are my memories."
Mog gulped. "That's the saddest thing I ever heard!"
"Maybe I shouldn't have buried the treasure, but I wanted to keep it safe," the pirate went on.
Mr. Bog started mopping up puddles on the stage again.
Mr. Freaky eyed the wet stage nervously.
"Er, today's Career Day assembly is over, students.
Let's thank Pedro the Pirate for his fascinating presentation."
All around Ben, monsters started clapping.
Mog pumped his fist in the air. "Yes, pirates!"
Pedro bowed. "Thank you, students," he said.
"I hope you all have your own merry bands one day.
You can sing jolly sea songs and search for pirate treasure!"
He waved and then bounded off the wet stage.
Mr. Freaky leaned over the microphone.
"That was certainly an exciting ending to this year's Career Day.
Pedro's career is fascinating.
Of course, being the principal at Monster Academy is just as exciting and satisfying as—"
Goosh! Water suddenly poured down onto the stage from above, soaking Mr. Freaky.
"Ack!" Mr. Freaky cried. His noses wiggled wildly.
"Mr. Bog! Some towels, please!"
Mr. Freaky took out his handkerchief and blew his noses.
"Don't worry, students. Everything is completely under control!"
"No, it's not," Ben said, looking at the puddles.
Mr. Freaky began drying himself off.
"It's lunchtime, students. Assembly dismissed!"
Ben headed to the lunchroom with his friends.
Along the way all the students were still talking about pirates and treasure.
"Pedro's career sounds awesome," Mog said.
"Much better than the dust collector's job."
Gaby laughed. "How would you know, Mog?
You were sleeping the whole time the dust collector talked!"
Mog ignored her. "Can you imagine sailing the seas with a pirate crew?
And filling a chest with gold and other loot?"
Gaby nodded. "That would be pretty amazing.
You could buy tons of scientific equipment, Waldo.
I know what I'd get—new detective books."
Winnie smiled. "I thought you might say you'd go on a dream vacation, Gaby."
"Nope." Gaby shook her head.
"I'm only dreaming about a library filled with mysteries."
Mog was still going on about Pedro's treasure chest.
"If we had all that loot, we'd all be rich—as rich as kings.
It’s too bad Pedro lost his treasure."
Winnie suddenly halted.
"That's it!" she said, snapping her fingers.
Ben looked at her. "What do you mean, Winnie?"
Winnie's eyes were glowing.
"Pedro said his treasure is lost somewhere in Monsterville," she said.
"But it doesn't have to stay lost. Let's try to find it!"
Mog blinked at Winnie.
"Uh, I don't get it, Winnie.
How can we possibly find Pedro's treasure?
The treasure map is gone, remember?
And Pedro buried that treasure chest a really long time ago."
"That's exactly why we might be able to find it," Winnie said.
"Because everyone else gave up looking a long time ago."
"Good point," Mog agreed. "I think it's a good idea."
Ben and his friends lowered their voices as they joined the other monsters in the lunch line.
"I don't know, Winnie," Waldo said.
"It sounds a little crazy, if you ask me.
It's like looking for a needle in a haystack—pretty much impossible."
Plop! A cafeteria troll dropped a serving of toad toes onto Ben's tray.
"Ugh." He made a face.
"They’re serving cold toad toes again?"
"Yeah," Mog said.
"That's all we ever get now—the cafeteria oven is broken."
"So is the dishwasher," Ben said, eyeing stacks of dirty trays.
"Well, I think Winnie's right," Gaby chimed in.
"Detectives find missing stuff all the time.
Maybe we can locate Pedro's treasure, even without the map."
"I suppose we could try using magic," Waldo said.
"What if I—ah-choo!"
All the monsters in the lunch line ducked as fireworks burst overhead.
"Hey, Waldo, you know the rule," a ghost said.
"No spells in the lunchroom!"
Gaby gave Waldo a sympathetic look.
"I guess that sneezing spell hasn't worn off yet, huh?"
"It's not a spell," Waldo insisted.
"I told you, I just have a cold."
"Sure you do," Gaby said. Waldo looked annoyed as she bent down to pat him on the shoulder.
Winnie led the way to a quiet table.
She gestured at the dripping ceiling and then at the floor, where a dozen buckets were lined up.
"We have to do something. This school is becoming a disaster zone."
A fish monster sat nearby, catching water drops in his mouth.
"Some monsters seem to like it," Mog said with a shrug.
"Well, if we did find the treasure," Winnie said, "we could use it to help fix up the school."
"Conditions are getting pretty bad," Gaby said.
"The kids over there are wearing winter coats and hats."
"Yeah, because it's freezing in here," Ben said.
"Just think. If we can find the treasure, we could make Monster Academy great again," Winnie said.
"I'm sure we can do it," Gaby said.
"We just need to think like detectives.
They solve problems by using deduction."
Mog shook up his carton of newt juice and took a big gulp.
"What's deduction?" he asked.
"It's examining clues and making smart guesses about what happened," Gaby said.
Ben nodded slowly.
"We might be able to find some clues about Pedro's treasure.
But it won't be easy."
Winnie put her hands over her ears as somebody started hammering on pipes somewhere nearby.
"Sorry, but we don't have time to search for clues to make deductions," she said.
"We need to find the treasure as soon as possible.
Magic will be much easier—and faster."
"I agree," Waldo said.
"Magic is definitely the way to . . ."
He pinched his nose to stop himself from sneezing again.
His face turned red and smoke billowed out of his ears.
"Deduction could be fast too," Gaby said.
"Yeah," Mog said. "Detectives on TV always solve cases fast."
"That's TV, Mog," Winnie said.
"In real life, detective work is slow and painstaking.
It takes a long time to figure out stuff."
"Well, we could try being detectives," Mog said with a shrug. "It would be fun."
"Yeah." Gaby nodded. "Lots of fun!"
Waldo shook his head. "Magic would be faster and better."
"I don't think so," Gaby said as Waldo sneezed again.
"Especially since you have that, um, cold."
Waldo cocked his head and looked at her.
"Want to make a bet—magic versus detective work?"
"Sure!" Gaby reached out her hand and grinned.
"I'm confident that detective work will work better than magic."
She shook hands with Waldo and then looked at the others.
"Who's on my team?"
"Me!" Mog said.
Waldo looked at Winnie and Ben.
"Well then, who wants to be on my team?"
He hiccupped and more smoke came out of his ears.
"I’ll be on your team," Winnie said.
"You might need some help with the magic."
"Uh-oh . . ." Ben gulped as all his friends turned to look at him.
"So, whose team are you on, Ben?" Gaby asked.
She drummed her fingers on the table, waiting for him to answer. "Mine or Waldo's?"
"Uh . . ." Ben looked at Gaby and Mog, and then at Waldo and Winnie.
Gaby was his best friend, but Winnie was his girlfriend.
Choosing teams was not going to be easy.
Ben stared down at his half-eaten toad toes.
"I'll help everybody," he blurted out.
"It's just a friendly bet anyway."
"Yeah," Mog said. "It's like a scavenger hunt.
We'll see who finds the treasure first."
"It's going to be us!" Gaby said, grinning.
Then she looked at Ben.
"But no sharing team secrets, okay, Ben?"
Ben held up his hands. "No problem."
"Who are you going to help first, Ben?" Winnie asked.
"I'll decide after I finish my lunch," Ben said quickly.
"We have study hall after lunch," Gaby said to Mog.
"Let's go to the library now and get started.
We can read about Monsterville history—that's the best place to start."
"Okay," Mog said.
The two of them returned their trays to the kitchen and hurried off to the library.
Winnie stood up. "Come on, Waldo.
We have to get started too.
Let's go to the lab and figure out a spell.
See you later, Ben."
Ben sighed as the two of them left.
"This situation stinks," he thought.
Somebody was bound to get mad at him.
Finally he decided he wasn't hungry anymore, so he picked up his tray.
As he headed toward the garbage can, a blob waved to him.
"Hey, Ben, are you going to eat those toad toes? I'm really hungry today."
"Nope. You can have them," Ben said.
"Just return my tray to the kitchen when you're done, okay?"
"Don't worry about that," the blob said. "I'll eat the tray too!"
"Great," Ben said. But he didn't feel great.
If only Gaby and Waldo hadn't made this stupid bet!
A few minutes later, Ben floated through the door of the science lab.
"How's it going in here?" he said.
Winnie looked up and smiled.
She was stirring a potion in a big cauldron as Waldo handed her some ingredients.
The liquid inside the pot glowed green as Winnie mixed it.
"We're brewing a location spell," she said.
"Can I help?" Ben asked.
"Sure." Winnie gestured toward some supplies on a high shelf.
"Can you hand Waldo that big sack of lizard scales?"
"The green ones or the gold ones?" Ben asked.
"Gold," Waldo said. "As in gold treasure."
"Got it." Ben had to use both hands to get the heavy sack off the shelf.
He lowered it and then handed the sack to Waldo.
"Ah-choo!" Waldo sneezed.
Ben and Winnie immediately braced themselves, but this time nothing happened.
Waldo grinned. "I think my cold is finally getting better!"
He tipped the sack and started to pour the lizard scales into the cauldron.
Suddenly Winnie yelped.
"Wait! Waldo! Ben gave you the green scales!"
She groaned. "Oh no. Now we'll have to start all over again."
"But . . ." Ben shook his head in confusion as he stared at the sack.
He was sure he'd given Waldo the right ingredient.
"I know I grabbed the gold—"
Winnie cut him off with a smile.
"On second thought, we're good," she said.
"We don't really need any help.
Like my mom says, too many witches spoil the potion.
Why don't you go see how Gaby and Mog are doing?"
Ben blinked at her.
He couldn't tell if she was trying to get rid of him or trying to be fair.
"Okay," he said with a shrug.
"See you later. Call if you need me."
As he left, he noticed that the bag of green scales was still on the shelf.
"I did get the right bag!" Ben thought.
"Waldo's sneeze must have changed the gold scales to green."
Ben felt annoyed. He'd tried to help Winnie, but Waldo had messed it up.
When Ben got to the school library, Gaby and Mog were already rushing out.
They were both grinning.
"You two look happy," Ben said.
"Did you find the treasure already?"
"Nope," Mog said. "But Gaby thought of a really good clue."
"I remembered that Pedro mentioned a painting," Gaby told Ben.
"He said an artist painted him before he buried the treasure."
"Right." Ben nodded.
"So that painting could hold a clue to finding the treasure!" Gaby said.
"We looked up information about pirate art," said Mog.
"And we found out where that painting is."
"Where?" Ben asked.
"At the Monsterville Historical Society," Gaby said.
"They've got some pirate artifacts there."
"We're going there after school," Mog added.
"You can come with us if you want."
"Okay . . . maybe," Ben said.
"If I'm not busy helping Winnie and Waldo."
After school Ben couldn't find Winnie.
So he went with Gaby and Mog to the Monsterville Historical Society.
The historical society was located in an old haunted house on the edge of town.
"Whoa, look at all this stuff," Mog burst out.
"Yikes," Ben added.
The ground floor of the building was packed with objects.
There were old toys and dusty books and racks crammed with robes, capes, and vests.
Huge mummies and wax monster figures stood along the walls of one room.
File cabinets overflowing with papers and old photographs filled another room.
Gaby scratched her head, looking overwhelmed.
"I hope we can find that painting of Pedro in here.
The building closes at six, and this could take longer than I thought."
"Maybe we can find a guide to help us," Ben said.
They looked around until they finally spotted a mummy wearing a guide badge.
Ben floated over to him.
"Excuse me, sir. We're looking for a specific painting of Monsterville," he said.
"It's an old painting showing Pedro the Pirate burying his treasure.
Do you know where it is?"
"Second floor. Outlaws section," the guide said.
"You can't miss it."
"Thanks," Gaby said. The three of them hurried toward the staircase.
"Hey, Waldo and Winnie just walked in!" Mog said.
"Why are they here?" Ben wondered aloud.
"Who cares?" Gaby said. "Come on. Let's find that painting!"
"You two can probably find it on your own," Ben said.
"I'll go say hello to Winnie and Waldo. Maybe they need some help now."
"Okay," Gaby said.
"But don't tell them about the painting. That's our clue."
"I will. I mean, I won't. Don't worry, Gaby.
I won't say a word about the painting."
Gaby and Mog tore upstairs.
Waldo and Winnie were still standing near the front entrance.
Ben floated up to them as they finished talking to a guide.
"Hi, Ben," Winnie said.
"How'd you know we were coming to the historical society?"
"I came with Gaby and Mog," Ben said.
"Oh. They're here too?" Waldo asked.
He sounded funny because he was pinching his nose to stop himself from sneezing.
"Did they find a clue that led here?"
"I can't talk about that, remember?" Ben replied.
"I'm helping both teams. What are you guys doing here?"
"We created a Magic Mirror spell," Waldo said.
"Huh?" Ben asked.
"It's a mirror for finding stuff. But the mirror works only one time," Winnie explained.
"We asked it to show us Pirate Pedro's gold."
"But it showed us an image of a golden compass from Pedro's pirate ship," Waldo said.
"The guide said the compass is definitely here—somewhere."
"When we find it," Winnie added, "we're going to cast another spell.
It'll take us to the burial site."
"Want me to help you look for the compass?" Ben asked.
"Okay," Winnie said. "The guide said it's in one of the back rooms."
"We're going to need to get permission to take the compass with us," Waldo said.
"Maybe you can talk with somebody about that?
We got Mr. Freaky to write a note."
Waldo handed Ben a sheet of paper.
"We told him we're working on a project about pirate ships."
"We didn't want to tell him about the treasure until we found it," Winnie said.
"No problem," Ben said.
"I'll go to the visitors' office. I think it's on the second floor."
Inside the visitors' office, Ben explained the situation to a bored-looking skeleton.
The skeleton barely looked at Mr. Freaky's note before stamping it, "Approved."
"Thanks," Ben said.
On his way back downstairs, Ben saw Gaby and Mog staring at a painting in a gold frame.
It showed Pedro as a young pirate skeleton.
He was standing on top of a chest inside a deep hole, looking proud as the sun sank behind him.
Nearby a few other pirates stood with shovels under a small oak tree.
Mog was quickly sketching the painting as Gaby wrote in a small notepad.
"Hey, Ben!" Gaby waved excitedly.
"We found the painting!" Mog said.
"We're not allowed to take a picture of it so I'm trying to draw it."
"We see a bunch of clues," Gaby said.
"Hmm." Ben looked carefully at the painting.
"All I see is the treasure chest, some pirates and Pedro, and a tree."
"Those are all clues," Gaby replied.
"The leaves on the tree show that it was early fall.
The position of the sun and the shadows tell us it was late in the day."
Mog's eyes gleamed.
"And the size of that treasure chest tells us something else—that treasure is huge!"
After studying the painting, Gaby and Mog went to look at some old maps of Monsterville.
Ben went back downstairs with the permission form.
He floated around, looking for Winnie and Waldo.
"Being on two different teams is exhausting," he thought.
"I hope somebody finds this treasure soon."
"Ben!" Winnie called to him from the front entrance.
"Did you get the approval? We found Pedro's compass!"
"Cool," Ben said. "And yes, you have permission to take it."
"Great!" Winnie said. "Let's go!"
The three of them dashed outside—and the sky instantly flashed with weird green light.
"Yikes!" Ben stopped in his tracks. "What's going on?"
"I think it's our spell," Waldo replied.
"We cast a magnet spell—it makes the compass attracted to Pedro's treasure."
Winnie held the compass in front of her as they hurried along Buzzard Place.
The compass needle seemed to be pointing at the Monsterville clock tower.
"Why didn't the first spell lead you right to the treasure?" Ben asked.
Waldo shrugged. "We don't know," he admitted.
"Although we did make a few mistakes with the potion, and I still have this dumb cold."
"Plus, I'm pretty new to spell casting," Winnie said.
They turned left at the clock tower, and the needle pointed them toward Swampside Lane.
By now the sky had grown dark.
A full moon hung over the bubbling green swamp as they raced along.
"Ah-choo!" Waldo sneezed a few times and had to slow down to catch his breath.
Ben was panting too.
"Why are you guys trying so hard to win?" he asked.
"It's only a friendly bet.
I mean, you're going to use the treasure to help fix the school, no matter who wins. Right?"
Waldo nodded. "Yeah . . ."
"So don't you think it's kind of dumb to try to prove that magic is better than detective work?" Ben went on.
"I mean, what's the point of arguing about it?"
Winnie burst out laughing. "It is kind of dumb," she admitted.
"But it sounded fun to me—like a scavenger hunt, as Mog said."
"Yeah," Waldo added with a grin.
"Besides, a wizard has to defend his magical powers.
Ah-ah-ah-choo!" He sneezed loudly, and the three of them turned green.
Winnie moaned. "Not again."
"Hey!" Waldo said. "I know! I'll cast a spell to fix my cold."
"No!" Winnie said sharply.
"No more spells for now. Let's just keep searching for the treasure."
Soon the compass was pulling the three of them up Cemetery Hill.
At the top they paused so that Winnie could reverse Waldo's green spell.
"Phew, that's better," Winnie said. "I didn't like being green."
Ben was staring down at all the lights below.
To the left he could see lights twinkling in People Place.
To the right Monsterville was lit up too.
"It's a nice view from up here."
"My parents hike up the hill sometimes," Waldo said.
"Enough small talk, guys." Winnie was staring at the compass.
"We're almost at the burial site." She pointed below.
"The compass is pointing down the hill, past that huge tree, and right at . . ."
Ben's eyes went wide as he realized where, exactly, the compass was pointing. "Monster Academy!"
Waldo gasped. "The treasure must be buried under our school!"
"Yep." Winnie took another look at the compass.
Sure enough, its needle pointed right at the school.
"Could it be wrong?" Ben asked.
"I don't think so," Waldo replied.
"I guess we'll find out," Winnie said.
Her voice shook. "I wonder what we'll find—piles of gold?"
Ben remembered the huge chest he'd seen in the painting of Pedro, but he didn't say anything.
That clue belonged to Gaby and Mog.
"Yes!" Waldo said.
"We're going to find tons of gold.
Maybe some other valuable stuff too, like pearls and jewelry.
Pirates stole all kinds of loot."
"Let's go," Ben said eagerly.
The three of them rushed down the hill and wound through the streets toward Monster Academy.
Even though school had ended hours ago, a few lights were on inside the school building.
"Someone's working late," Ben said.
"Maybe Mr. Bog is still mopping up all those puddles."
"Or trying to fix the heat again," Winnie said.
Just then Ben spotted some figures near the big tree close to the front of the building.
One of the figures was very tall.
"It's Gaby and Mog!" he said.
"Looks like they tracked the treasure here too!"
"Hi, guys!" Winnie called to Gaby and Mog.
They looked up in surprise.
"Hey!" Gaby said. "Did you guys track the treasure here too?"
Waldo smiled at her. "Yep."
"We followed some clues in an old painting at the Monsterville Historical Society," Gaby said.
Then she gestured at the old tree.
"There was a tree in the painting. We think it might be this one."
"It's grown a lot since Pedro buried the treasure," Mog said.
Winnie held up the gold compass.
"We found Pedro's old compass and put a spell on it.
I guess it worked just as well as detective work."
"Which means everybody is a winner!" Ben said brightly.
"So you guys don't have to compete anymore. We're all on the same team now."
"That was so much fun," Mog said.
"We still need to find the treasure," Winnie reminded everyone.
"All we know is that it's buried near this tree," Gaby said.
She glanced at the school building.
"Maybe it's even buried under the school building."
"That's what we were thinking too," Waldo said.
"We can try using the compass to track the exact spot."
