assure you that everything is totally under control, Mayor!" "It had better be, Freaky!" Mayor Hubbletree patted
his son's head. "Just sit back and enjoy the show,
Mayor!" Mr. Freaky hurried away. After Ben's family sat down, Sid pointed upward. "Look
at all those balloons!" Ben looked up. A large net holding colorful balloons hung from
the ceiling. "Maybe they'll drop the balloons at the end
of the performance," Dad said.
"Or they could be for one of the acts," Sid said. "What are the acts anyway?" Ben
shrugged. "Who knows? Everything about the circus is a big secret." "Good evening, madam!" Oliver
Scribblebottom suddenly popped up
in front of Ben's mother
with his camera. "Tell me—how do you feel about attending the first-ever people-monster
circus?" "Oh!" Ben's mother said, startled. "I'm, um, very excited!" Just then Cleo hurried across the
stage to lay down a pair of stilts. Ben waved to her,
but she just stared straight ahead. "That weird expression again,"
Ben thought. "It's driving me
crazy!" He glanced at the clock on the wall. He had ten minutes before
the show started—plenty of time to find Ronny
and ask him some questions. Ben jumped up, telling
his parents he was going to the restroom. Then he wove through the crowd and slipped backstage,
where the ringmaster was pacing around, studying some notes in his
hand. Ben floated toward him. "I don't know what you're doing to the performers, Ronny, but you're not
going to get away with it!" Ringmaster Ronny looked up, startled. "You
again!" he snapped. "How dare you forget the wrath of the circus!" "I
don't care about the wrath
of the circus!" Ben said. "You've done something to my friends, and
I want to find out what it is!" "That's absolutely true!" Ronny said, laughing loudly.
"I've turned
them into circus artists. I admit I had my
doubts about working
with monsters at first, but they have proven to be
surprisingly well-behaved." "Well-behaved?" Ben said.
"They're acting like zombies." Ronny chuckled. "Your friends may not seem like themselves right
now, but that's because they've been
working so hard. Trust me,
young man, er, ghost, there's nothing to worry about—except getting a good seat for the show. Huck!"
He waved to the crew member. "Please escort this young ghost back to his
seat!" Huck put down a piece of equipment and headed toward Ben. "I'm going! I'm going!"
Ben said, floating away fast. Just then he saw Sarah talking quietly to
Zork. "You'll be fine, Zork," Sarah murmured. "Trust
me." Zork shook his head. "It's so high!" "Of course it is. It's a
high wire!" "But . . . but . . . " Zork clutched
his stomach, suddenly looking very green—even for a
lizard monster. "Oh, for Pete's sake!" Sarah
muttered. "Follow me, Zork." As Sarah spun around, Ben
ducked behind a rack of costumes. Peeking through the clothes, he saw Sarah leading Zork out into
the hallway. "Where are they
going?" Ben wondered. There was only one way to
find out. With a quick glance
backward to make sure Huck hadn't followed him, Ben floated after them. Sarah led Zork
to a quiet spot in the hallway. "You won't fall, Zork, I
promise." Zork paced around, looking upset. "Can you stop pacing for a moment?"
Sarah said. "I just need to—" "I quit!" Zork started to walk away, but
Sarah caught his arm and pulled him back. "Zork,
look into my eyes." "What's she doing?" Ben thought, floating closer. "Look
into your eyes?" Zork squirmed to get away. "Why?" "I just want to say .
. . " She looked directly into his eyes. "Sludge!" Instantly Zork stopped squirming. "Whoa!" Ben thought.
"He looks just like Cleo when she was twirling Waldo
on her finger." Then he realized Zork looked
just like something else—Sid's zombie impression!

episodes.title: The Show Must Not Go On!

subtitle.text: Ben stared at Sarah Swingwire. "She's hypnotizing Zork!" he realized. "Maybe
she's hypnotizing all of the circus performers!"
"You're ready now, Zork," Sarah said. "Go back into the gym, and wait for the circus to start." Without
a word, Zork turned and headed back toward the gym. He took small careful
steps, as if he was walking on a high wire. Ben
shot over to Sarah. "Did you just hypnotize Zork?" "What?" Sarah blinked in surprise. "No, of course
not." "I saw you!" Ben said. "When you said 'sludge,' Zork went into
a trance." "I . . . I
. . . " Abruptly Sarah spun around. "I'm getting out of this
place! Enjoy the show!" "I
can't let her leave," Ben thought. "Not before I find out what's going on!" He zoomed down
the hall, taking a shortcut so he could reach
the main entrance ahead of Sarah. Then he ducked into a dark corner
of the lobby. Just before Sarah reached for the doors,
he jumped out in front of her. "Boo!" "Ahh!" Sarah screamed and put
a hand to her heart. "You monsters are always scaring me!" Ben scowled at her. "Tell me—why were you hypnotizing Zork?" "Fine." Sarah took
a deep breath. "Ronny was really excited about the circus,
especially after Oliver Scribblebottom decided to make a movie about it. I wanted the circus
to be a success too, but I . . . " "Go on," Ben said impatiently. Sarah was
still breathing hard. "But I had never worked with monsters before,
and I was really nervous. So I hypnotized the performers to protect
myself—and make sure the circus went well for Ronny's sake.
I didn't tell him about it because
I was worried he'd fire
me. But it all turned out to be a big mistake."
"What do you mean?" Ben asked. She bit her lip. "Monsters become super focused or act weird when
they're hypnotized. Yesterday Mog refused to get out of the cannon. And Maddy
kept grabbing other students and juggling them!" "Maddy had better not do that tonight—especially with the mayor's son sitting
in the front row," Ben murmured. "I've had to hypnotize Zork three times today," Sarah went on. "If he suddenly
snaps out of it while he's up on the tightrope . . . " She gulped. "Sarah, you have to
stay and help me stop the show," Ben said. "It's too late." Sarah glanced at
her watch. "The circus starts in one minute!" "One
minute?" Ben thought fast. How could they fix this? Suddenly he remembered Cleo's odd behavior again.
"You trained the performers to go into a trance whenever somebody says the word 'sludge,'
right?" Sarah nodded. "How do you snap them out
of it?" he asked. She quickly explained. "Come on!" Ben cried. "Let's go
before the show starts!" Together they raced
down the hallway. But as they approached the gym, Ben could hear
circus music coming from inside. Then the crowd burst into
loud applause. "We're too late!" Sarah cried. "Try it anyway!" Ben yelled.
"Do what you always do to snap a performer out of a trance!" Sarah nodded and began blowing
huge bubbles with her gum, popping them like crazy. But
inside the gym, the crowd was
roaring so loudly, the performers couldn't hear the popping sound. "Ugh," Ben groaned. This wasn't working. He looked around the gym for a
second. "You keep popping bubbles," he said to Sarah. "I've got another idea!"
He shot over to Jen and Gaby's seats on the floor. "Isn't this
fun, Ben?" Gaby said. "I can't
wait to see Winnie perform!" "Actually, I'm trying to stop Winnie—and everyone else—from performing." Ben told Jen and Gaby about Sarah. "Oh no!" Jen cried. "That's terrible. What
should we do?" "If we work together, we may
be able to fix everything." Ben filled
them in on his plan. Jen and Gaby
exchanged looks. "That sounds a little crazy," Jen said. "Right,
Gaby?" Gaby glanced up at the
ceiling. "It sounds more than a little crazy," she said. "That's exactly why it
just might work!" "Jen, go find
Waldo and tell him what to do," Ben said. "Hurry!" "Got it!" she said. As she
rushed off, a cheer rose
from the audience. Ben turned to see Zork
climbing the ladder that led to the high wire. "Gaby, we have to hurry too!" Ben
said. "Come on!" The two of them raced up to the top of
the risers. Ben noticed that in one corner, a rope was tied to a
hook on the wall. He untied the knot and looked over at Gaby, who
stood on the other side of the riser. She finished untying
her knot and then
nodded at Ben. As they both let go, Ben held his breath. "This has to work!" he thought.
Ben watched the net of balloons carefully, still holding his breath.
But to his dismay, nothing happened. He looked over
at Gaby and realized that a knot
in the rope prevented the net
from falling. She was stretching as high as she could, but
she couldn't reach the knot. She waved Ben
over. "You can reach
it," she mouthed. Ben zoomed over to the knot. Below,
the audience in the risers began to cheer and clap. Zork had
reached the other side of the high wire without falling. "Hooray!" a
goblin shouted. "He did it!" "That's a relief!"
Ben thought as he started working on the knot. Unfortunately, it was slow
work. The rope had frayed, and Ben's fingers trembled as
he tried to undo the tight knot. "Ugh!" he
groaned. "This is going to take forever!" "You can do it!"
Gaby called up to him. "Don't
give up!" A
second later an amazed gasp rose from the
crowd. Ben looked down to see Maddy juggling
dodo eggs with her tentacles. She stepped down from the stage and
began walking, mixing among the audience members who were
sitting near the front of the stage. For a moment the crowd seemed to enjoy her
act. Then— whoosh! Maddy
shot out one of her tentacles and grabbed a small, three-eyed monster. The tiny
monster cried in surprise as Maddy tossed him into the air with the dodo eggs.
"Hey!" he yelled. "Stop juggling me! I'm not a dodo egg!" The monster's mother
jumped to her feet. "Mr. Freaky! Do something!" "Oh
dear!" Mr. Freaky tried to get close to Maddy.
One of her tentacles knocked him over. "Ben, hurry!" Gaby urged.
"I'm trying!" Ben said.
"I'm going as fast as I
can!" For the next minute, Ben worked on the knot while stealing quick
glances at the scene below.
The audience watched uneasily as Maddy juggled dodo eggs and the young monster.
A surprised shout rang out when she
suddenly reached into the crowd
again, grabbing a second monster
child. Sarah Swingwire raced toward Maddy, desperately waving her arms and snapping her gum
to get the octopus monster's attention. But it
was no use. The crowd was still too loud, and
Maddy was paying no attention to Sarah. By now her eyes were locked on something
else in the crowd—little Timothy Hubbletree. "That octopus monster wants to juggle me!" Timothy shouted. Mayor Hubbletree leaped
to his feet, frantically trying to shield Timothy from Maddy's flying tentacles. "Freaky!"
the mayor yelled furiously. "If anything happens to my son,
you're in big trouble!" Mr. Freaky stood back
up, his noses wiggling. "Stop juggling those children right now, Maddy!" Maddy didn't
seem to hear him. The principal looked at Ringmaster Ronny. "Why
is Maddy acting like this? Is this part of her act?"
The ringmaster shrugged. "I don't
know what's going on. We've never worked
with monsters before. And we probably never will again!" Ben swung back to the knot. He'd
almost untangled it when
the crowd below went completely silent. A chill ran up
Ben's spine. Now what was happening?
A new act had started. Deb hung upside down from the trapeze bar by her knees,
holding Winnie by the arms
and swinging her back and forth. When Deb let go, Winnie was supposed
to sail
toward another trapeze bar. But as Deb swung her, Winnie missed—and sailed out over the audience! Ben
gasped. "Winnie!" he shouted. "No!" Everyone in the room seemed
to hold their breath until Winnie
somehow managed to reach out and grab one of the metal rafters
running across the ceiling. "Whew!"
Ben said. Thank goodness Winnie was safe. Mr.
Freaky rushed to the microphone onstage. "Please calm
down, everyone." He blew his noses. "There's
nothing to worry about—everything is totally under control!" "Are
you kidding?" Mayor Hubbletree shouted. "Nothing is under control here! Every time I come here,
there's total chaos!" "Mayor Hubbletree is right," Ben thought. He
guessed he had only seconds before the gym really did
descend into total chaos. Finally he untied the knot. "Yes!" he
cried as the net swung open. The stunned
audience looked up, mesmerized as hundreds of colorful balloons drifted down toward them. Ben
drew in a breath, frantically trying to locate Waldo
in the crowd. At last he spotted him—standing
in perfect position in front of the risers. "It's
up to you now, Waldo," Ben thought.
"Please don't mess this up!" Waldo waved his
wand and— poof! Little Timothy turned
into a porcupine!
"Oh no!" Ben cried. "That's it!" Mayor Hubbletree shouted. "This place is
a . . . a . . . circus!"
